la:adj:inofficiosus.html:
ĭn-offĭcĭōsus, a, um, adj.,
undutiful, inofficious.
In gen.
Not observant of his duty, undutiful: humana gens inofficiosa dei,: libertus inofficiosus patrono,.—
Contrary to one's duty: testamentum, i. e. one in which nothing is left to one's nearest relatives, children, etc.,; cf. .—
In partic., not obliging, disobliging: in aliquem,.

senses: deprived, lacking, needy (+ genitive or ab + ablative)
la:adj:inops.html:
ĭnops, ŏpis, adj.
2. in-opis
,
without resources, helpless, weak (class.).
In gen.: ab ope inops, qui ejus indiget, Müll.: inopes relicti a duce,: nihil cum potentiore juris humani relinquitur inopi,: solare inopem et succurre relictae,.—
With ab: sic inopes et ab amicis, et ab existimatione sunt,. —
With inf.: inopes laudis conscendere carmen,unable, (3, 1, 23 Müll.).—
In partic., helpless through poverty, destitute, needy, indigent.
Lit.: res pauperes inopesque,: aerarium inops et exhaustum,empty,: te semper inops vexet cupido,unsated,: domus cujusvis inopis,. —Esp., of the dead who could not pay Charon's fee: haec omnis inops inhumataque turba est,; cf.: infletaeque jacent inopes super arva catervae,: mortuis in ore nummum immittere, ut apud inferos non tamquam inopes errent, Schol. . —
With gen., destitute of, without: humanitatis,: amicorum,: animi,: mentis,: consilii,: rationis,: senatus auxilii humani,: terra pacis,: somni cibique,: provinciae virorum,: miles Martis,that never fights,.—
Plur. as subst.: ĭnŏpes, um, opp. potentes, Dietsch.— Sing.: si nihil cum potentiore juris humani relinquitur inopi,. —
Trop.
Of inanimate things, mean, wretched, contemptible: inopis et pusilli animi esse,: nostras inopes noluit esse vias,: advorsus atque inops amor,: odia aegra sine armis errabant, iraeque inopes,impotent,: vita,. —
Of speech, poor in words or ideas, meagre: non erat abundans, non inops tamen,: non inops verbis,: ad ornandum,: Latinam linguam non modo non inopem, sed locupletiorem etiam esse quam Graecam,: vir inopi lingua et infacundus,.

la:noun:inopia.html:
ĭn-ŏpĭa, ae, f.
inops
,
want, lack, scarcity.
In gen.: argenti,: summa rerum omnium,: frumenti commeatusque,: frumenti,; cf.: frumentaria,: et amore pereo et inopia argentaria,: loci,: advocatorum,: consilii,: criminum,: occasionis,: remedii,: veri,—
In partic., a want, esp. of necessaries, want, need, indigence, scarcity, fewness.
Lit.: opem ferre inopiae, i. e. to one in want, : Quor (me) conducebas? Bal. Inopia; alius non erat,: ne inopiam cives objectare possint tibi,: si propter inopiam in egestate estis,: utrum propter imbecillitatem atque inopiam desiderata sit amicitia,; cf.: amicitiam ex inopia atque egestate natam volunt,; so also with egestas,: in Rhodiorum inopia et fame summaque annonae caritate,: inopiae subsidium,: inopiam vitare,: ad pudendam inopiam delabi,: inopiam alicui facere,to bring one to want,: manuum mercede inopiam tolerare,: multorum dierum inopia contrahere pestem,: dispensatio inopiae,of scanty supplies,.—
Transf.
Want, helplessness: praesidio esse contra vim et gratiam solitudini atque inopiae,to those who have no protectors,: in hac causa improbitatem et gratiam cum inopia et veritate contendere,; ; : judicum,worthlessness,: ingenti cum difficultate itinerum locorumque inopia,and the want of necessaries in these regions,; .—
Of a speaker: inopia et jejunitas,poverty of ideas,.—
Of the want of fruition: incendere animum cupidum alicujus inopiā,.

la:adj:inopinus.html:
ĭn-ŏpīnus, a, um, adj.,
unexpected (poet. and in post-Aug. prose = in-opinatus, insperatus): quies,: nova inopinave facies laborum,: fors,: visus,: siccitas,; .

la:verb:inolesco.html:
ĭn-ŏlesco, lēvi, ŏlĭtum, 3, v. n. and a.
(inolesti, § 36).
Neutr., to grow in, on, or to any thing.
Lit.: udo libro,: necesse est multa diu concreta modis inolescere miris,; : tradux a materno sustinetur ubere dum inolescat,.—
Trop.: assidua veterum scriptorum tractatione inoleverat linguae illius vox,i. e. had remained fixed in his mind,: quae nosti, meditando velis inolescere menti,.—
Act., to implant: natura induit nobis inolevitque amorem nostri et caritatem,: alicui semina amoris inolesti (= inolevisti),: inolitum nomen urbi, Mai.: in moribus inolescendis,.
la:verb:inolesco.inflection: lēvi, ŏlĭtum, 3, v. n. and a.

la:adj:inoffensus.html:
ĭn-offensus, a, um, adj.,
not struck; without stumbling, without hinderance, unobstructed, uninjured (poet. and in postAug. prose).
Lit.: cogit inoffensae currus accedere metae,untouched, not grazed,: voluptatis regionisque abundantiam inoffensa transmitteres,: inoffensum pedem referre,not stumbling,.—
Transf., that goes on without hinderance, without obstacle, unhindered, uninterrupted: lumen oculorum,: inoffensae metam tangere vitae,placid, undisturbed,: sed mare inoffensum crescenti adlabitur aestu,: oratio,: cursus honorum,: litterarum inter se conjunctio,: copulatio vocum,: tantā temperantiā (vir) ut omnia fere vitae suae tempora valetudine inoffensa vixerit,.— Adv.: ĭnoffensē, without stumbling, without hinderance, Ambros. Apol. David, 3, § 9; , Serm. 10, 43; .—Comp.: inoffensius,.

la:adj:inordinatus.html:
ĭn-ordĭnātus, a, um, adj.,
not arranged, disordered, irregular: inordinati et incompositi milites,: hostes,: inordinati in proelium ruunt,: ordo, Oud. — Sup.: inordinatissimi pili,.—In neutr. absol.: idque ex inordinato in ordinem adduxit,disorder,; ; ; .—Adv. in two forms.
ĭnordĭnātē, irregularly: febres redire,; so 1, 4. —
ĭnordĭnātim, irregularly: acies non inordinatim incedebant, .

la:adj:inopinatus.html:
ĭn-ŏpīnātus, a, um,
not expected, unexpected (class.).
Adj.: cum hoc illi improvisum atque inopinatum accidisset,: nova tibi haec sunt et inopinata?, § 24: neque novum neque inopinatum mihi sit,: nec hoc tam re est, quam dictu inopinatum atque mirabile,: malum,: finis vitae,: fraus,: id quoque scriptum est, quod volgo inopinatum est,contrary to the common belief,.—Sup.: inopinatissim us sensus,.—
Subst.: ĭnŏpīnātum, i, n., something unexpected: nihil inopinati accidit,.—Hence, ex inopinato, adverbially, unexpectedly: aliae ut ex inopinato observant,: repente ex inopinato prope cuncta turbata sunt,.—Adv. in two forms.
ĭnŏpīnātē, unexpectedly: aliquem inopinate occupare,.—
ĭnŏpīnātō, unexpectedly: in castra irrumpere,.

la:adj:inornatus.html:
ĭn-ornātus, a, um, adj.,
unadorned (syn. incomptus): mulieres,; cf. capilli,; ; and, crines,: Lysias tenuis atque inornatus,; so ; ; : nomina et verba,plain, common,: non ego te meis Chartis inornatum silebo,uncelebrated,.— Adv.: ĭnornātē, without ornament, inelegantly: dicere,.—Comp.: inornatius scribere, Fronto ad Verum Imp. ep. 1 med. Mai.

la:adj:inopportunus.html:
ĭn-opportūnus,
unfitting (late Lat.),

Oros. c. Pelag. p. 618 (also a false reading in two places for importunus, ; ). — Hence, ĭnopportūnē, adv., unsuitably, untimely, Aug. c. Faust. 22, 72.

la:verb:inoboedio.html:
ĭn-ŏboedĭo (or ĭnŏbaudĭo, ), īre, v. n.,
to disobey, be disobedient, . — Hence, ĭnŏboedĭens, entis, P. a., disobedient, ; . — Adv.: ĭnŏboedĭenter, disobediently, , 14, 17.

la:verb:inopinor.html:
ĭn-ŏpīnor, ātus sum, 1, v. dep.,
to suppose, think, opine: Alexander facilius inopinatus, Val. Res Gest. Alex. M. 1, 52 Mai. (but a false read. for opinor,).

la:adj:inopinabilis.html:
ĭn-ŏpīnābĭlis, e, adj.,
not to be supposed or expected, inconceivable: latebra,: id (dictum),: res,.—
Esp., rhet. t. t., surprising, paradoxical: infames materias, sive quis mavult dicere inopinabiles, quas Graeci ἀδόξους ὑποθέσεις appellant, veteres adorti sunt, .—Adv.: inŏpīnābĭlĭter, unexpectedly, ; .

la:adj:inopinans.html:
ĭn-ŏpīnans, antis, adj.,
not expecting, unaware (freq. in the historians; not in Cic.): inscios inopinantesque Menapios oppresserunt,: impeditos et inopinantes aggressus,: imprudente atque inopinante Curione,: rex in potestatem inopinanti (ei) venerat,: suis inopinantibus,.— Hence, adv.: ĭnŏpīnanter, unexpectedly, .

senses: not pleaded or heard (in a court)
la:adj:inoratus.html:
ĭn-ōrātus, a, um, adj.,
not pleaded: incertā re atque inoratā, i. e. without obtaining a hearing, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 12 Vahl.): legati Ameriam re inorata reverterunt,.
